title: Coalesce Advisor: signal-fusion profiler for continuous batching thermostat
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Build a lightweight advisor service that fuses multiple workload signals to synthesize continuous batching and caching parameter recommendations. The advisor will run profiling sketches, evaluate heuristic candidates, and create safe gradual rollout plans (shadow -> canary -> full) with automatic rollback gates.
problem_statement: Current automated batching tooling proposes static batch profiles that either underutilize GPUs during low load or cause latency regressions during short bursts and KV-cache misses. Engineers spend manual effort tuning min/max batch sizes, max_wait_ms, and cache prefetch heuristics per workload. We need an automated system that learns from live signals and produces conservative, safety-guarded config changes.
goals: Produce per-workload continuous batching parameter recommendations (min_batch, max_batch, max_wait_ms, kv_window_hint)
Expose a safety-first rollout plan for each recommendation: shadow -> staged canary -> full apply
Automate metric gates and rollback for regressions in latency, error rate, and quality
Ship observability for decision rationale so SEs/PMs can audit and override recommendations
non_goals: Replace model-level quality evaluation (LLM output QA) - we only provide hooks to integrate eval triggers
Complex RL-based optimizer in first iteration
Auto-apply without stakeholder approval for P0 customers
proposal_summary: The Coalesce Advisor will run a streaming profileer that computes compact workload sketches (request size distribution, prefix reuse rate, KV cache hit proxy, inter-arrival distribution, p50/p90/p99 latency baselines). A signal-fusion layer combines these into an uncertainty-aware score that drives candidate parameter generation. Each candidate is validated via a low-impact shadow test and then a staged canary with metric gates. A thermostat controller continuously tweaks parameters within conservative bounds to keep GPU utilization and latency SLOs near targets.
technical_design: Profiler: 15m sliding windows producing fingerprints: token_length_histogram, prefix_reuse_fraction, kv_hit_estimate, arrival_peaks, burst_index
Signal fusion: weighted ensemble of heuristics + Bayesian uncertainty estimate (thin-client implementation using precomputed weights)
Candidate generator: map fingerprints -> parameter space using rule-templates (min_batch, max_batch, max_wait_ms, kv_prefetch_factor)
Shadow runner: route 2-5% traffic with candidate config in parallel (no effect on production routing) and collect cost/latency/quality deltas
Canary ramp: automated staged rollout 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% with metric gates at each step (latency p99, error-rate, quality proxy, cost-per-token), default step time 30m
Thermostat controller: PID-like loop that adjusts max_wait_ms and target batch size based on target_utilization (default 0.7) and observed tail latency
Safe-apply engine: pre-checks for model compatibility & kernel suitability; abort if candidate increases memory pressure beyond threshold
Rollback policy: immediate auto-rollback on gate failure plus a human-review path for intermittent regressions
Observability: per-recommendation rationale, profiler snapshots, shadow/canary run results, and exact config diffs in console
acceptance_criteria: Advisor creates a reproducible recommendation and rollout plan for at least 80% of profiled workloads in the staging cluster
Shadow runs show no more than 5% degradation in p99 latency compared to baseline for recommended candidates in 90% of cases
Automated canary pipeline performs staged rollouts with metric gating and can perform rollback without manual intervention
Recommendation UI surfaces reason strings and the top 3 signals that drove the decision
End-to-end tests and a chaos scenario (sudden spike) confirm thermostat controller nudges parameters conservatively and respects SLOs
milestones: M3: Shadow runner + telemetry ingestion into console — 2026-04-12
M4: Canary automation + metric gates + rollback — 2026-04-26
M5: Thermostat continuous tweak loop + production pilot — 2026-05-10
tasks: Implement lightweight profiler agent (Go) + sampling policy
Design signal-fusion schema and tunable weights
Build a candidate rule-template library based on SKU and model family
Integrate shadow runner into router to mirror requests safely
Implement canary pipeline in rollout service and define gate thresholds
Add UI panels in Console: recommendation card, diff viewer, shadow/canary timeline
Write unit/integration tests + create staging pilot with 5 teams
Document runbook for manual override and incident response
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Shadow tests may under-represent edge bursts. Mitigation: Require stress-synthesis sampling and synthetic bursts in simulator before canary
Risk: False-positive regressions trigger unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: Use aggregated windows and hysteresis before auto-rollback; allow manual override
Risk: Thermostat oscillation causing parameter thrash. Mitigation: Add damping, min-duration constraints, and step-size caps
Risk: Model/kernel mismatch when applying aggressive batching. Mitigation: Pre-check kernel suitability and memory headroom; fallback to safer variant
open_questions: What is the default weighting across signals (latency vs cost vs prefix-hit) for first rollout?
Do we need per-customer safety multipliers for enterprise SLAs?
Should the advisor expose an API for external orchestration systems to query candidate confidence?
observability_plan: Profiler metrics exposed as time-series with tag cardinality capped (workload-id, model-family)
Recommendation audit trail persisted with snapshots for 30 days by default
Shadow/canary run metrics pushed to Console with diff visualizations (cost delta, latency delta, error delta)
Slack/Email alerting for canary gate failures and automatic rollback events
qa_plan: Create synthetic workloads (short prompt, long prompt, prefix-heavy) and run regression matrix
Run nightly stochastic simulation against historical traces to validate advisor stability
Perform blast radius testing in staging with forced kernel regressions and verify rollback
notes: This effort should be coordinated with Runtime (kernel selection) and Console teams. Start with non-critical workloads (not P0) for pilot. Estimate assumes two engineers + one SRE half-time for three sprints.
